title: Learning Experiences
text:
SELECTING LEARNING
 EXPERIENCES
 KICD
What are learning experiences?
Learning experiences refer to the activities or tasks
that the learner should carry out in order to develop
desired knowledge, skills, values and attitudes
Learning experiences focus on developing the learner’s
cognitive, physical and emotional domains.
How can the teacher select learning experiences?
• Selection of learning experiences should be based on specific
 learning outcomes. The learner should achieve the intended specific
 learning outcomes after active engagement in the selected learning
 experiences.
• Flexibility- Other than the suggested learning experiences in the
 designs, the teacher is free come up with other learning experiences
 according to the unique needs of their learners and the school.
• Learning outcomes are achieved through learner-centred activities.
Contd.
The teacher should make appropriate choices when selecting
learning experiences for the achievement of given curriculum
outcomes by:
Breaking the learning outcomes into teachable units according to ;
• Allocated number of lessons
• The learning outcomes stated in the sub-strand
• Available resources (both materials, tools, equipment & resource
 persons)
• Integration of ICTs as a learning tool is critical to build digital
 literacy
Contd.
• Innovative approaches to cater for needs of all learners
  individual/ group activities
• Teaching strategies:
  cooperative learning
  peer tutoring
  team teaching
  activity based teaching etc.
• The core competency to be developed in the lesson
• The value(s) to be developed in the lesson
All these strategies help in achieving the targets set for the
learners.

Learning experiences that enable the learner to acquire
Digital Literacy competencies include:
a)Guided use of the internet
b)Manipulating ICT devices eg camera, laptop etc.
c)Watching recommended video clips
d)Using digital devices to back-up their work
Learning experiences that can enable the learner
to acquire knowledge
a)Peer work
b)Individual work
c)Field trips
Learning experiences enable the learner to acquire
skills
a) Project work /practical work
b) Field work
c) Small group discussions
d) Case studies
Learning experiences enable the learner to acquire
desired values /attitudes
• Interaction with others during the learning
 experiences –so that the learner can model the
 value(s)
Learning Experiences and Methodologies
In the Competency-Based Curriculum, different methods are suggested to
facilitate learning. These methods include:
a) Question and answer
b) Group discussions
c) Problem solving
d) Experiments
e) Dramatization
f) Role play
g) Debates
h) Reflection
i) Practical activities
j) Research
k) E-Learning
Types Of Learning Experiences
• Formal learning experiences
• Non-formal learning experiences
• Informal learning experiences
Formal learning experiences
• Organized within classroom or other school contexts (e.g. the field,
 school garden etc.)
• The learning experiences are dictated by learning outcomes in the
 curriculum design
• Below is an example showing the link between the specific learning
 outcome and the learning experiences
NOTE: The learning experiences must address each one of the stated
specific learning outcomes
Non-formal Learning Experiences
• These are critical for the learner to continue applying what
 s/he has learnt in scenarios outside the classroom.
• This include clubs and societies. The learner is able to apply
 knowledge/skills/values and attitudes they have learnt
 formally outside the class in club activities eg
 o Speaking skills in debate clubs
 o Drawing/painting/modelling skills in Art club
 o Singing/dancing skills in Music club
 o Performing skills in Drama club
Informal learning experiences
• Entails general social interactions at school, home and in the
 wider community.
• The community plays a key role in shaping the moral
 nature/compass of the learner
• These experiences offer the learner a forum to model values
• How can members of the community help the learner to
 model values?
 oBeing role models in behaviour moderation in the learner
 oMass media (print & audio-visual) should vet the content
 available to the youth
In summary….
In CBC, the teacher should not take centre stage in the learning process.
The role of the teacher is to facilitate learning by giving the learner an
opportunity to take responsibility for their learning.
Learning experiences enable the learner to:
a) acquire and apply knowledge and develop skills, values and attitudes
b) Acquire and apply the intended core competences
c) Model the core values
d) self-regulate and evaluate their learning
e) engage deeply in the learnt concepts
f) reflect on the learning process
g) interact with others during the learning process
